# Comparisons

This folder contains structured comparison articles derived from the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB) annual reports. It covers national, regional, and hospital-level performance across clinical quality indicators, including antibiotic administration times, CT scan turnaround, surgical response times, epidural usage, and mortality rates stratified by Charlson comorbidity scores. Each page reconstructs the original data tables, highlights leaders and trailers, tracks longitudinal trends where available, and identifies statistical outliers in Danish acute surgical care.

## Pages

- [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] — Tracks overall patient volumes and surgical intervention rates across multiple reporting periods, highlighting fluctuations in the total patient population and the proportion of operated versus non-operated patients.
- [[fordeling-af-alder-for-opererede-01-09-2022-31-08-2023|"Fordeling af alder for opererede, 01/09/2022 - 31/08/2023"]] — Compares the age distribution, including quartiles and means, of operated patients across Denmark, its five regions, and individual hospitals to highlight demographic burdens.
- [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] — Evaluates the proportion of patients receiving antibiotic treatment within three hours of arrival, revealing widespread failure to meet the national standard across all regions and hospitals.
- [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] — Measures 90-day mortality across Danish healthcare units against a national development target, highlighting significant outliers like Rigshospitalet and varying regional compliance.
- [[indikator-10c|Indikator 10c]] — Tracks the 30-day mortality rate for highly comorbid patients (Charlson Score ≥ 3), showing universal failure to meet clinical standards and high volatility in small-sample hospitals.
- [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] — Assesses the proportion of patients receiving a CT scan within two hours of arrival, showing universally poor performance with no region or hospital meeting the ≥ 90% target.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Compares the proportion of patients receiving a CT scan within two hours of arrival, highlighting significant disparities between major university hospitals and smaller facilities.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Analyzes regional performance for preoperative optimization or direct-to-surgery pathways, showing a systemic shortfall where all regions miss the ≥ 90% standard.
- [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]] — Compares national and regional performance metrics, revealing a marked geographical spread between the highest-performing Region Nordjylland and the lowest-performing Region Sjælland.
- [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] — Evaluates regional performance against a ≥ 90% development target, showing that both leading and trailing regions fall short of the required threshold.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Measures the proportion of patients operated on within six hours of arrival, revealing a systemic failure to meet the 80% target across all five Danish regions.
- [[indikator-5x|Indikator 5x]] — Tracks the proportion of patients operated on within six hours for perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, highlighting a systemic challenge in acute surgical response times.
- [[indikator-5y|Indikator 5y]] — Evaluates the proportion of acute surgical patients without perforation, ischemia, or bleeding operated on within six hours, showing universal failure to meet the 90% standard.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Tracks the epidural insertion rate across Danish regions and hospital units, showing wide variation and a national average that misses the > 60% target.
- [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] — Evaluates the fulfillment of epidural administration standards across seven Danish hospitals, highlighting dramatic improvements at some facilities and stagnation at others.
- [[indikator-9b|Indikator 9b]] — Measures the 30-day mortality rate among patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2, highlighting significant variation across regional and local hospital units.
- [[indikator-9c|Indikator 9c]] — Evaluates 30-day mortality for highly comorbid patients (Charlson Score ≥ 3), providing insight into outcomes for high-risk populations across different hospital units.
- [[indikatoropfyldelse-efter-region-og-hospital|Indikatoropfyldelse efter region og hospital]] — Details the regional and hospital-specific fulfillment rates for Indikator 1 (antibiotics within 3 hours), including confidence intervals and historical year-over-year comparisons.
- [[median-tid-fra-ankomst-til-sygehus-til-modtagelse-af-antibiotika-minutter|Median tid fra ankomst til sygehus til modtagelse af antibiotika (minutter)]] — Compares the median time in minutes from hospital arrival to antibiotic administration, revealing extreme delays and wide quartile spreads at specific hospitals.
- [[oversigt-over-alle-indikatorer|Oversigt over alle indikatorer]] — Provides a structured framework of the ten specific clinical quality metrics used to monitor acute surgery, detailing their types, formats, and national standards.
- [[resultater-for-indikator-11-mortalitet-indenfor-90-dage-efter-akut-kirurgi|"Resultater for Indikator 11: Mortalitet indenfor 90 dage efter akut kirurgi"]] — Analyzes 90-day mortality rates following acute surgery, identifying specific hospitals that failed to meet the < 20% national clinical standard.
- [[supplerende-indikator-til-10b-mortalitet-indenfor-30-dage-efter-akut-kirurgi-hvis-charlson-score-1-eller-2-alle-opererede|"Supplerende indikator til 10b: Mortalitet indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi, hvis Charlson Score = 1 eller 2. Alle opererede."]] — Tracks 30-day mortality for patients with mild to moderate comorbidities, showing significant historical volatility and universal failure to meet quality standards.
- [[supplerende-indikator-til-indikator-9a-mortalitet-indenfor-30-dage-efter-akut-kirurgi-hvis-charlson-score-0-alle-opererede|"Supplerende indikator til indikator 9a: Mortalitet indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi, hvis Charlson Score = 0. Alle opererede."]] — Compares 30-day mortality for patients with no severe comorbidities, isolating surgical outcomes and highlighting major outliers like Rigshospitalet.
- [[supplerende-indikator-til-indikator-9b-mortalitet-indenfor-30-dage-efter-akut-kirurgi-hvis-charlson-score-1-eller-2-alle-opererede|"Supplerende indikator til indikator 9b: Mortalitet indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi, hvis Charlson Score = 1 eller 2. Alle opererede."]] — Analyzes 30-day mortality for patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2, revealing increased mortality risks compared to baseline and varying regional trends.
- [[supplerende-opgoerelse-af-asa-score-for-opererede-boxplot|"Supplerende opgørelse af ASA-score for opererede, boxplot"]] — Maps the ASA physical status classification levels across Denmark's five healthcare regions, concluding that differences in preoperative comorbidity burdens are not statistically significant.
- [[supplerende-opgoerelse-over-fordelingen-af-cancer-01-09-2022-31-08-2023|Supplerende opgørelse over fordelingen af cancer 01.09.2022 - 31.08.2023]] — Breaks down the distribution of cancer diagnoses among acutely operated patients, revealing that the vast majority of surgical cases involve no cancer diagnosis.
